text: The function \(f(x) = x + |x|\) is continuous for
solution: For \(x\ge 0\), \(f(x)=x+x=2x\); for \(x<0\), \(f(x)=x-x=0\). Each piece is a polynomial, and at \(x=0\) the left-hand limit \(0\), the right-hand limit \(0\) and the value \(f(0)=0\) all agree, so \(f\) is continuous there too. Hence \(f\) is continuous for every real \(x\), that is \(x\in(-\infty,\infty)\). Hence (A).
